items.title: Mary Bonnet Reveals Plans to Move Out of L.A After 'Selling Sunset' Exit
items.summary:
After leaving Selling Sunset , Mary Bonnet revealed she is also planning to move away from Los Angeles.

“We’re likely moving to Nashville,” Mary, 46, told TMZ on Friday, November 20. “The real estate market here is horrible.”

Mary noted that after 25 years in Los Angeles, she was looking for a “more peaceful life.” She also cited her work with animal rescues and how it influenced her lifestyle. 

“I’m not good at just sitting idle and although I’m not sitting with the dogs, I need more land because I have a lot of them,” she said. “We’ve had 13 at one point.”

Selling Sunset's Mary Bonnet Reveals How Show 'Hurt' Her Career Before Exit 

She continued: “I’m starting a rescue of my own. I started off fostering and I started seeing the problems in the system and … once you see it, you can’t unsee it.”

Mary joined Selling Sunset when it premiered in 2019. The reality series became an overnight success for Netflix as viewers were introduced to employees at high-end Los Angeles real estate brokerage The Oppenheim Group.

Earlier this year, Mary shocked viewers when she made the decision to step away ahead of season 10.

“This show actually hurt my real estate business,” she revealed exclusively to Us in July. “I went into Selling Sunset thinking it was going to help — and in the beginning it did.”

The reality star admitted she struggled in her career, adding, “It hasn’t hurt Jason [Oppenheim], but he’s removed from all the drama. Anything they did — even though I was removed from it — still impacted my career. I lost a lot of clients and I lost a lot of deals because of it.”…
items.t: Mary Bonnet Reveals Plans to Move Out of L.A After 'Selling Sunset' Exit

Brielle Biermann got candid about the pros and cons of growing up in the public eye with her Bravo star mom, Kim Zolciak .

“I definitely want to be my own person. I think that was kind of the theme here today with everybody,” she exclusively told Us on set of Celebrity Weakest Link ’s “Next Generation” episode, which also included Joseph Baena, Sailor Brinkley-Cook, Cori Broadus, Corinne Foxx, Prince Jackson, Hailie Jade Scott and Melissa Rivers . “I am Brielle Biermann first and Kim’s daughter second.”

Biermann, who recently tied the knot with Billy Seidl in Florida, is determined to pave her own way. 

“I want people to remember that and know that I have my own identity,” she noted. “So I’m trying to be more conscientious about those types of shows or opportunities and decisions going forward so that way I can really branch out and be my own person.”

Paltrows! Levys! Kardashians! See Famous Celebrity Families’ Photos 

Before competing for her charity of choice — World Central Kitchen — on the Fox game show, Biermann and her family were featured on The Real Housewives of Atlanta from 2008 to 2012. Zolciak, 48, subsequently received her own spinoff show titled Don’t Be Tardy for the Wedding , which focused on her nuptials with Kroy Biermann . The series was later renamed to Don’t Be Tard y and continued to air until 2020.

Having her life featured on reality TV taught Brielle some important lessons.

items.title: Sharna Burgess Claims 'DWTS' Fans Use Votes to 'Manipulate the Show'

In a recent Instagram Story, Burgess, 41, replied to a fan who asked whether she was surprised when Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Johnson were sent home during the semifinals.

“Sadly no, I felt it was going to be another shock elimination,” Burgess wrote. “Not because they deserved it but simply because the online discourse is so wild that [it] was pretty clear who fans were ‘voting off’ and how they have felt about dance experience contestants.”

Burgess continued, “[It’s] so disappointing to see our voting system is now being used by viewers to vote people off instead of voting for your favorite. I say we got [sic] back to yall only have 10 votes total and you have to figure out how to dish them out.”

items.title: Fina Strazza Calls Amy Poehler ‘Dig’ Audition a ‘Dream Come True’

Strazza, 21, exclusively spoke with Us about the upcoming series and what it meant to work alongside comedian Amy Poehler and Parks and Recreation cocreator Mike Schur .

“I remember finding out that I was going to be doing a chemistry read with Amy and just being like, ‘Even this is a dream come true, I can’t imagine being considered to be able to actually do the show for real,’” Strazza told Us .

Fresh off her acclaimed performance in John Proctor Is the Villain , which earned the young actress a 2025 Tony Award nomination, Strazza says the role landed her in Schur and fellow showrunner J.J. Philbin ‘s “orbit” after the pair watched her in the Broadway production.

The opportunity was especially meaningful for the actress, who called Poehler, 55, and Schur, 51, “heroes” after growing up watching Parks and Recreation and Saturday Night Live with her sister, Nixie.

“When I knew I was going to be part of the show, [Amy] sent out an email being like, ‘We’re so excited you are Patty, and we’re all going to be best friends, and I can’t wait,’” Strazza told Us .

items.title: Donny Osmond Makes Rare Comment About Michael Jackson Child Abuse Claims
items.summary:
Donny Osmond made a rare comment about the child molestation allegations that continue to cloud the legacy of his late childhood friend Michael Jackson .

In an interview with the U.K.’s Guardian newspaper published on Monday, November 23, Osmond, 68, was asked if he believes “there was truth in the allegations” against Jackson, who died at age 50 in 2009.

“I’m not going to go there. I don’t want to go there. Because he was such a dear friend,” the Osmonds singer said.

Osmond conceded that the allegations took a toll on Jackson in his final years.

'Leaving Neverland' Director Claims Michael Jackson Was 'Worse' Than Epstein 

“I think a lot of things destroyed him. The pressure destroyed him, too — the expectations of all the people around him. There’s only so much blood in our veins,” he said. “Every time I’d go over, he’d be like: ‘How’s your family, tell me this, tell me that,’ because he realized I had something he didn’t have: normalcy. It’s sad. We lost a genius.”

Jackson was first investigated over the alleged abuse of a then-13-year-old Jordan Chandler in 1993. No charges were ever filed against Jackson, who denied the allegations, and he later reached an out-of-court settlement with Chandler and his parents after they filed a civil lawsuit against the King of Pop.

Greg Doherty; Christina Barany/Getty Images 
 More than a decade later, Jackson was acquitted of child molestation charges during a high-profile 2005 trial.

Since Jackson’s death, more accusations have been made against him. The 2019 HBO documentary Leaving Neverland detailed claims made by Wade…
items.t: Donny Osmond Makes Rare Comment About Michael Jackson Child Abuse Claims
